steps.prompt: $218$ children and $173$ adults go to a show. About how many people is that? You have $5$ seconds.

cards.title: Round first
cards.body: An estimate is a quick, close answer. Round each number to a friendly number, then add or subtract: $218 + 173 \approx 200 + 200 = 400$. The exact answer is $391$, close to $400$.

cards.title: Worked example: 47 + 38
cards.problem: Estimate $47 + 38$ by rounding each number to the nearest ten.

steps.text: The estimate is $90$. The exact answer, $85$, is close, so it is sensible.

cards.title: How close?
cards.body: Each number moves a little when you round. $47 \to 50$ moves up $3$, $38 \to 40$ moves up $2$: the estimate is $5$ too big. When both round up, the estimate is too big; when both round down, too small.

prompts: When would an estimate be good enough, and when do you need the exact answer?
